intent: Generate compact Section 2 location-discovery proposals; no new hero
reference: User-attached city/state/course-wise discovery screenshot and Careers360 first-party location navigation; palette H2

prompts.name: Architectural Destination Shelf
prompts.layout: Concept L1 / Architectural Destination Shelf. Single horizontal row of SIX open illustrated city tiles. Each has a refined, accurate warm architectural landmark illustration (high-quality editorial digital illustration with subtle realistic material shading, not cartoons or 3D plastic toys), on a small rounded ivory/greige inset with very thin outline. Each city tile around230px wide and185px tall. Linework plus quiet wine/taupe shadow details makes the illustrations beautifully cohesive without flattening landmark character. Each tile's city name below the illustration and a small wine arrow on the same baseline; a very small Explore colleges link below. No huge white card body or heavy shadows. Tiles align perfectly, equal content height, some illustrations use curved arch upper edge but labels all outside on plain backgrounds. BELOW a slim warm-white band carries Browse by state left and the six state name chips with modest map-pin line icons; All states right. No geographic state silhouette accuracy needed. Heading, subtitle and little course-context dropdown in the first100px. Main visual rail and states take only400px total. This is creative through architectural art direction and precise navigation, not another generic college photo-card grid. Light background edge contours tie the scene together. No featured city monopolises width.
prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a high-fidelity flat front-facing desktop screenshot of a COMPACT DOWNSTREAM SECTION of the NSEDU Indian education homepage. The user already has an approved header and hero above. This section is the next content block: STUDY DESTINATIONS / COLLEGES BY LOCATION, inspired by the useful city/state discovery rows in the user's education-site screenshot. It is NOT a new landing page or hero. Do not show a navbar, logo header, search hero, giant headline, student lifestyle hero photo or signup banner. No essay, charts, college fee cards or long ranked tables. Content is browsing destinations and moving to college/course details.
Canvas: an unusually wide and SHORT website section screenshot, approximately 1700px wide x 650px high, panoramic 2.6:1. Present one cohesive compact section with about36px vertical padding and48px side margins. Desktop content heading approximately32px, body16px, city names20px and chip labels15px. Do not inflate typography into poster-sized hero lettering to fill the image. The visible section should feel about520px tall when used on a normal1440px desktop website. Rich useful information but calm breathing room.
LOCKED NSEDU palette: primary wine #72243B; accent warm taupe #806C60; light ivory #FFFAF8; soft greige #F1ECE8; white surfaces; dark text #2A2024. Heading type resembles DM Serif Display and body Plus Jakarta Sans. The warm ivory background has very subtle curved taupe edge contours and a faint campus linework corner, only6-8% opacity and away from text; beautiful designed backdrop with absolutely no crowded ornament, no glass, no neon, no blue interface or green buttons. Natural landmark/photo colours allowed. Fine borders and small rounded14px corners, subtle hover cues, wine arrows, professional clickable destination affordances. Landmarks identify geography, not college campuses. No invented college counts, rankings, cheapest/safest claims, sponsorship ads or scholarship figures. No slogans on buildings, books, bottles or floating motivational text.
Exact main heading "Explore where you want to study". Supporting line "Choose a city or state to explore colleges, courses and fees." Heading left and "View all locations →" right. A SMALL course-context control reads "Course: All courses" with dropdown chevron, not a big new course-selection section. Optional secondary quicklink "Choose a city" in the footer, no GPS/current-location request. Six city entries exactly "Delhi NCR", "Bengaluru", "Mumbai", "Hyderabad", "Pune", "Chennai"; no unsupported count under them, use "Explore colleges →" as action text where layout allows. Landmarks: Delhi India Gate; Bengaluru Vidhana Soudha; Mumbai Gateway of India; Hyderabad Charminar; Pune Shaniwar Wada; Chennai Central Station. Keep geography labels correct and English spelling exact.
Under the main city discovery row, a SECOND much shallower state navigation row headed "Browse by state", containing "Maharashtra", "Karnataka", "Telangana", "Tamil Nadu", "Uttar Pradesh", "Madhya Pradesh" and a small "All states →" link. These are navigation choices not a claim of complete sourced catalog coverage. Include restrained footer explanatory text "Your course choice carries into location results." Tiny outside-UI concept label and "Visual concept · NSEDU" in an unobtrusive corner. These are visual proposals, no live counts or promises.
The result should look like professional editorial navigation in the middle of a polished education website. Creative visual treatment, useful content and concrete clickable choices. Do not decorate with random widgets. Only prescribed functional text.

prompts.name: Editorial City Postcards
prompts.layout: Concept L2 / Editorial City Postcards. Distinct visual treatment: a SIX-column row of elegant small destination PHOTOGRAPHIC postcards with shallow landscape ratio, each realistic warm daylight photo of the exact corresponding landmark. Each postcard uses a gently rounded top and a slim white label footer with city name on left and burgundy circular arrow on right. One selected tile (Pune) has a thin wine outline and a subtle Selected marker; other tiles neutral and consistent. Not huge full-height city posters. Course context dropdown in top-right under View all locations. BELOW cards one slim active-context ribbon reads "Pune selected" with a secondary button "Explore colleges in Pune →" and short text "Review courses, tuition and admission details." This is explicitly the selected location state and must correspond to Pune tile. State links sit below the ribbon as a single thin text navigation row with separators (not a second photo-grid). Headline remains32px and photo rail is150-180px high. Overall around520px page height, beautifully art-directed colours and clean aligned content. No fake Pune stats, ratings, city living-cost estimates or hostel guarantees. Creative postcard-style browsing with a clear next action, not a new travel landing page.

prompts.name: Two-Row Location Atlas
prompts.layout: Concept L3 / Two-Row Location Atlas. A truly different organisation without a huge side image: top-right a small segmented switch "Cities" active / "States", course-context dropdown next to it. Main content SIX destination entries as a THREE-column by TWO-row grid. Each entry is a compact horizontal clickable tile, around470x105px, with a beautiful small landmark vignette illustration occupying100px on left, then city name20px, a single-line caption "Explore colleges, courses & fees", and wine arrow aligned far right. The illustration is clipped within an elegant quarter-arch or circle segment, not circular city photo badges. Tiles have white backgrounds and extremely fine taupe edges; the city rail grouping sits on one subtle greige shallow section backdrop with no giant map. Bottom a narrow Browse by state row with six text links and All states, no photos. Small functional helper "Start with a location. Keep your course preferences." near footer may replace the common footer to avoid repetition. Header compact and block overall about500px tall. Creative landmark vignettes and horizontal geometry create professional rhythm while it is immediately readable. Do not add geographic map boundaries, numbers or every city's name repeatedly. The switch is a navigation state preview, not a separate section. No arrow lines spanning city tiles, no giant manifesto heading.
